coverage_note: November additions cover Nature Portfolio research and 2026 NeurIPS, ICML and ICLR papers. Each entry gives its source date and publication status; earlier work remains available for comparison. Original registry totals retain their existing cutoff.

assessments.headline: Models learn across signals, devices and longer records
assessments.summary: xMAE uses ECG-PPG timing, BioX-Bridge transfers between signals and EEG-X transfers across headsets. HEARTS and EmoPhone test reasoning and changes in recording conditions.
assessments.limit: Results are task-specific; the wearable-API study reports weak substance-use and craving prediction even after personalization.

assessments.headline: Personal health data enter coaching and movement feedback
assessments.summary: The Personal Health Agent coordinates analysis and coaching. EEG movement-error detection supplies a feedback signal for stimulation systems.
assessments.limit: These new studies measure conversation quality and laboratory error detection; treatment outcomes remain reported with the existing trials.

assessments.headline: Personal models update when new measurements arrive
assessments.summary: The ICU glucose twin tests fast patient adaptation and error-triggered updates. Earlier diabetes work links model updates to daily feedback and treatment support.
assessments.limit: The new ICU study uses ten patients' retrospective glucose recordings; the evaluated output is a short-horizon forecast.

assessments.headline: Wearable input stays stable longer, and clothing adds touch displays
assessments.summary: Dry electrodes reduce repeated calibration, implanted magnets track muscle mechanics and pixel fibres combine display with touch input.
assessments.limit: The new studies evaluate research interfaces and prototypes; the magnetic-control experiment uses a virtual prosthetic cursor.

signals.title: The anatomy of a personal health agent
signals.before: Single-agent PHIA or parallel specialists answer using the same Gemini backbone.
signals.after: A coordinator brings together wearable-data analysis, health knowledge and personal coaching.
signals.evidence: Experts rated overall conversation quality at 72.8%, compared with 54.4% for PHIA and 64.3% for parallel agents.
signals.limit: The live study used 45 people role-playing 50 health-data personas; the outcome was conversation quality.
signals.implication: Personal health assistants can connect calculations with advice, with response quality and latency assessed together.
signals.availability: Research implementation and evaluation materials released by the authors.

comparison.baseline: Single-agent PHIA and parallel specialists, using the same Gemini backbone.
comparison.result: Expert overall quality: 72.8% for PHA, 54.4% for PHIA and 64.3% for parallel specialists.
comparison.conditions: Role-played health conversations; reported in the PHA evaluation and Supplementary Tables 38-39.

signals.title: Touch-sensing digital pixel fibre enables interactive garment GUI
signals.before: Fibre displays separated display circuitry from touch localization.
signals.after: One fibre architecture combines individually addressable LEDs, connections and touch sensing in a garment sleeve.
signals.evidence: The prototype has 96 × 54 pixels, 8-bit colour and 30 frames per second, with touch input and wireless image transfer.
signals.limit: The 30-frame rate is for video without audio; synchronized audio-video was demonstrated at 25 frames per second.
signals.implication: Clothing can display information and accept touch input at the same surface.

signals.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
signals.before: Changes at the electrode-skin contact can force muscle-signal decoders to be recalibrated.
signals.after: Breathable carbon-nanotube dry electrodes maintain skin contact and reduce drift and movement artifacts.
signals.evidence: The multichannel EMG interface maintained task performance for 14 days without decoder retraining after minutes of initial training.
signals.limit: The result concerns the tested electrophysiology interface and recording conditions.
signals.implication: Stable sensing hardware can reduce the calibration work required for long-term body-input systems.
signals.availability: Research electrodes made with a roll-to-roll process.

signals.title: A digital twin for tracking and forecasting glycemia with septic patients in ICUs
signals.before: A fixed model forecasts without checking when an individual's signal patterns have changed.
signals.after: A pretrained PatchTST model checks new glucose readings and adapts when forecast errors require an update.
signals.evidence: Ten septic ICU patients were evaluated after pretraining on one patient's data. Thirty minutes of readings supported 15- or 30-minute forecasts; personalization took seconds on a laptop.
signals.limit: The retrospective study tested inpatient glucose forecasts; dosing decisions remained outside the evaluated workflow.
signals.implication: A personal model needs a defined update rule, a prediction horizon and a way to check its errors.
signals.availability: Research workflow evaluated on hospital continuous-glucose recordings.

signals.title: Using error-related brain activity to identify mismatches during virtually simulated and electrically stimulated upper-limb movements
signals.before: A stimulation controller needs feedback about whether its movement matches the person's intended movement.
signals.after: EEG measures responses to mismatches between intended arm movements and an avatar or electrically stimulated movement.
signals.evidence: Five volunteers completed discrete-movement tests and 16 completed continuous-movement tests. At the best tested feature window, electrical-stimulation classification accuracy averaged 91 ± 13%.
signals.limit: Participants were able-bodied. Continuous-movement classifiers used large mismatches and unequal error/no-error trial counts.
signals.implication: Detected movement errors provide a signal that future stimulation controllers could use for feedback.
signals.availability: EEG, avatar and electrical-stimulation laboratory setup.

signals.title: Limited utility of consumer wearable APIs for predicting substance use and craving, despite model personalization
signals.before: Personalization is often used to adapt a general model to one person's wearable history.
signals.after: The study compares global supervised, global self-supervised and personalized self-supervised models on Fitbit heart-rate and step data.
signals.evidence: Sixteen participants supplied 47 substance-use or craving prediction scenarios. Mean AUROC across the model approaches ranged from 0.569 to 0.617.
signals.limit: The results concern six substances and the signals available through the tested consumer API.
signals.implication: Choose sensor access around the target task; model adaptation alone may add little when available signals carry little relevant information.
signals.availability: Published analysis of wearable records collected in daily life.

signals.title: A wireless magnetic implant system for continuous neuromuscular sensing
signals.before: EMG interfaces infer movement from muscle electrical activity.
signals.after: A skin-mounted array tracks 3-mm implanted magnetic beads to measure muscle movement directly.
signals.evidence: Three participants with below-knee amputations controlled a virtual ankle-foot cursor. The system tracked beads at depths up to 6 cm with sub-millimetre resolution.
signals.limit: Participants controlled an on-screen cursor representing prosthetic movement; walking with a physical prosthesis was outside this experiment.
signals.implication: Muscle mechanics offer another input alongside electrical signals for assistive-device control.
signals.availability: Research system with implanted magnets and an external wearable sensor array.

signals.title: EEG-X: Toward Device-Agnostic and Noise-Robust Foundation Models for EEG
signals.publication_status: Accepted conference paper; manuscript updated 10 Nov 2026
signals.before: Changing electrode layouts makes it difficult to reuse an EEG encoder across headsets.
signals.after: Channel locations and reconstruction of cleaned activity help the encoder transfer across sensor layouts.
signals.evidence: Across eight datasets and five headset configurations, one TUAB-to-BCICIV_2A test reached 37.58% balanced accuracy, compared with REVE's 35.91%.
signals.limit: This comparison freezes the pretrained encoder and trains a linear classifier under the paper's transfer protocol.
signals.implication: Teams can evaluate a shared encoder across different headset layouts.
signals.availability: Public manuscript revised 10 November; NeurIPS 2026 conference presentation is in December.

comparison.baseline: REVE pretrained for the same TUAB transfer protocol.
comparison.result: BCICIV_2A balanced accuracy: 37.58% versus 35.91%, a gain of 1.67 percentage points.
comparison.conditions: Frozen encoders with linear evaluation; latest manuscript Table 3.

signals.title: EmoPhone: A Multi-Wave Dataset for In-the-Wild Mobile and Wearable Affect Sensing
signals.publication_status: Accepted, Evaluations and Datasets Track; manuscript updated 11 Nov 2026
signals.before: A single collection period gives little evidence about transfer across different annual study waves.
signals.after: Android and Fitbit recordings cover three annual waves, with tests across people, time and collection waves.
signals.evidence: The dataset includes 282 people, 297 participant-wave records and 53,139 momentary self-reports. Fourteen people returned in later waves.
signals.limit: In the latest full paper, adaptation improves its MLP backbone while supervised tree models remain competitive.
signals.implication: Benchmark across changing users and collection conditions before choosing a sensing model for daily use.
signals.availability: Public dataset repository and revised manuscript; NeurIPS conference is in December.

signals.title: Inertia-1: An Open Exploration of Wearable Motion Foundation Models
signals.before: Sampling rate, sensor position and model design differ across studies, making results difficult to compare.
signals.after: A shared experimental framework compares sensing and pretraining choices using over 18.2 million hours of accelerometer data.
signals.evidence: Evaluation spans 15 datasets, including activity recognition, freezing-of-gait detection and disease prediction.
signals.limit: The evaluation uses task-specific activity, gait and disease-prediction tests.
signals.implication: Select sensing settings and training objectives using comparisons across the tasks your application needs.
signals.availability: Public code and data-processing recipes; accepted at NeurIPS 2026.

signals.title: Physiology-Aware Masked Cross-Modal Reconstruction for Biosignal Representation Learning
signals.before: Pretraining often treats ECG and PPG as interchangeable views, losing their physiological timing relationship.
signals.after: Masked reconstruction across ECG and PPG teaches a model to preserve the delay between heart electrical activity and the peripheral pulse.
signals.evidence: The paper reports stronger performance than unimodal and multimodal baselines on 15 of 19 downstream tasks.
signals.limit: The 19 tasks include cardiovascular outcomes, laboratory results, sleep stages and demographic attributes.
signals.implication: Known relationships between sensors can guide pretraining and improve transfer across devices.
signals.availability: Published conference paper and public code; first manuscript posted 1 May.

comparison.baseline: Unimodal and multimodal representation-learning baselines in the paper.
comparison.result: Higher performance on 15 of 19 downstream tasks.
comparison.conditions: Task-specific evaluations with device, body-site and acquisition-setting transfer; formal proceedings abstract.

signals.title: HEARTS: Benchmarking LLM Reasoning on Health Time Series
signals.before: Medical question answering alone leaves sensor interpretation and multi-step temporal reasoning untested.
signals.after: HEARTS separates perception, inference, generation and deduction across 110 health time-series tasks.
signals.evidence: Sixteen datasets cover 12 health domains, 20 signal types and more than 20,000 test samples. General language models trail specialist models as reasoning becomes more complex.
signals.limit: Results compare health-signal tasks; the formal conference version evaluates 14 language models.
signals.implication: Evaluate signal understanding and calculations separately when building a health-data assistant.
signals.availability: Published proceedings, benchmark and public manuscript.

signals.title: SleepLM: Natural-Language Intelligence for Human Sleep
signals.before: Sleep analysis commonly assigns predefined stages or event labels to recording segments.
signals.after: SleepLM aligns physiological recordings with text and learns caption generation alongside signal reconstruction.
signals.evidence: Training uses over 100,000 hours from more than 10,000 people. Evaluations include retrieval, descriptions and language-guided event localization.
signals.limit: The model uses polysomnography and sleep-text data; these inputs differ from a consumer watch's summary API.
signals.implication: Sleep interfaces can support questions and descriptions as well as fixed-stage classification.
signals.availability: Published conference paper; captioning pipeline, checkpoints and architecture are released.

signals.title: BioX-Bridge: Model Bridging for Unsupervised Cross-Modal Knowledge Transfer across Biosignals
signals.publication_status: Published main-conference paper; manuscript revised 24 Feb 2026
signals.before: Knowledge distillation trains a student while repeatedly running a larger teacher model.
signals.after: A small bridge connects intermediate representations across body-signal models, using paired recordings without target-task labels.
signals.evidence: Across the tested ECG, PPG, EEG and EMG transfer tasks, trainable parameter counts fall by 88% to 99% while transfer performance is maintained or improved.
signals.limit: Tests cover stress, freezing-of-gait and sleep-wake recognition with paired source and target recordings.
signals.implication: Adapting an existing model to another sensor can require fewer trainable parameters.
signals.availability: Published ICLR 2026 proceedings; first manuscript appeared in October 2025.

comparison.baseline: The paper's cross-modal transfer and knowledge-distillation methods.
comparison.result: 88% to 99% fewer trainable parameters, with maintained or improved task performance.
comparison.conditions: Unsupervised target-modality adaptation using paired ECG, PPG, EEG and EMG recordings.

signals.title: HiMAE: Hierarchical Masked Autoencoders Discover Resolution-Specific Structure in Wearable Time Series
signals.before: Using one time resolution can lose either brief physiological events or longer patterns.
signals.after: A hierarchical encoder and decoder reconstruct masked recordings and expose features at several time scales.
signals.evidence: The study evaluates classification and signal generation, and reports sub-millisecond inference on smartwatch-class CPUs.
signals.limit: On-device timing depends on the tested CPU and model setting.
signals.implication: Choose a feature time scale around the task while accounting for the wearable device's compute budget.
signals.availability: Published ICLR 2026 proceedings; first manuscript appeared in October 2025.

signals.title: GlucoFM: A Dual-Stream Foundation Model for Continuous Glucose Monitoring
signals.publication_status: Accepted main-conference paper; linked to existing GlucoFM record
signals.before: Earlier glucose encoders provide one combined representation of a daily recording.
signals.after: Separate streams model the underlying glucose level and short-term deviations, while masks retain missing-data information.
signals.evidence: Pretraining uses 109,066 hours from 477 participant/session records. Across four cohorts, mean PR-AUC is 58.8 versus 54.7 for CGM-JEPA retrained on the same corpus.
signals.limit: The classification comparison uses participant-separated cross-validation and the same linear classifier.
signals.implication: The existing GlucoFM entry now links to its accepted conference paper and matched-corpus comparison.
signals.availability: Public manuscript and code; the original repository record is retained.

comparison.baseline: CGM-JEPA retrained on the same pretraining corpus.
comparison.result: Average PR-AUC: 58.8 versus 54.7 on the paper's reported percentage scale.
comparison.conditions: Four evaluation cohorts, participant-separated cross-validation and matched linear-classifier evaluation; Table 3.
